cards.front: MgSO₄ for fetal neuroprotection before 30 weeks is a 4 g IV loading dose, then a [___] infusion until birth or for up to 24 hours.
cards.context:
MgSO₄ given antenatally for imminent preterm birth <30 weeks reduces cerebral palsy in survivors by ~30% (Cochrane). Mechanism is uncertain — possibly preventing glutamate excitotoxicity in the immature brain.

Regimen: 4 g IV loading over 20-30 min, then 1 g/h infusion for ≥4 h before delivery — aim as close to 4 h before birth as possible.

NNT ≈63: treat ~63 mothers to prevent one case of cerebral palsy. A modest absolute benefit, but cheap and low-risk, so given routinely at this gestation.

cards.front: The inguinal ligament extends from the anterior superior iliac spine to the [___].
cards.context: The inguinal ligament extends from the anterior superior iliac spine to the pubic tubercle. Its inrolled edge forms the canal floor.

cards.front: Transvaginal cervical length ≤25 mm at [___] weeks defines a 'short cervix' and substantially raises spontaneous preterm birth risk.
cards.context:
Use transvaginal ultrasound to confirm suspected short cervix. In the current WA pathway, low-risk screening starts with transabdominal assessment at the 18-20-week anatomy scan.

If transabdominal length is under 35 mm, confirm transvaginally. A confirmed 21-25 mm prompts vaginal progesterone and repeat scanning; shorter measurements need specialist review.

cards.front: Newborn blood spot screening is performed at [___] hours by heel prick; a positive screen is not a diagnosis and needs confirmatory testing.
cards.context:
Collected at 48-72 hours, after milk feeds are established, so markers such as phenylalanine in PKU have had time to rise. If the baby goes home earlier, arrange collection.

Coverage 25+ conditions: endocrine (congenital hypothyroidism, CAH), metabolic (PKU, MCAD, MSUD), CF, immunodeficiency (SCID) and SMA. Thalassaemia is not on the Australian panel.

Document consent; a positive screen triggers recall for confirmatory testing.

cards.front: A woman who has never given birth at 20 weeks or more is described as [___], even if she has had miscarriages.
cards.context:
Parity counts previous births at 20 weeks or more (or 400 g or more), live or stillborn. Twins count as one birth.

Miscarriages and terminations before 20 weeks add to gravidity but not to parity.

cards.front: Reduced or absent smell with congenital GnRH deficiency is [___] syndrome.
cards.context: Kallmann syndrome is congenital GnRH deficiency with a reduced or absent sense of smell. Olfactory and GnRH neurons migrate together, so both functions are lost when that fails.

cards.front: At 16 weeks, a woman without a previous diagnosis has BP 140/90 mmHg on two occasions four hours apart, with elevated ambulatory readings. Urine and organ-function tests are normal; the classification is [___].
cards.context: Hypertension first identified before 20 weeks is classified as chronic, even without a previous diagnosis. Gestational hypertension is the trap: it begins after that boundary.

cards.front: During total laparoscopic hysterectomy, the colpotomy ring delineates the vaginal [___].
cards.context: The fornix surrounds the cervix at the top of the vagina. A ring seated there marks where the cervix can be separated from the vagina while preserving the vaginal walls.

cards.front: Intrapartum antibiotic prophylaxis for women with risk factors is given to reduce neonatal [___].
cards.context:
The organism is already in the birth canal. Labour and birth are when the baby meets it, so the antibiotic is timed to that passage rather than to a clinic visit.

The effect claimed is fewer babies with early-onset group B streptococcal disease. It is prophylaxis for the newborn, not treatment of a maternal fever.

cards.front: A woman with no previous miscarriages attends an early pregnancy clinic with bleeding and a confirmed viable intrauterine pregnancy. Progesterone is not offered: for threatened miscarriage it is reserved for women with [___] or more previous miscarriages.
cards.context:
RANZCOG (C-Gyn 38): with threatened miscarriage and no more than one previous miscarriage, progesterone is not recommended; it makes little to no difference to live birth.

NICE NG126 offers it after one or more previous miscarriages, following a Cochrane review that found a modest benefit at that threshold. RANZCOG reserves it for two or more.

reference.title: Miscarriage, Recurrent Miscarriage and Ectopic Pregnancy (C-Gyn 38)

cards.front: On day 4 after birth, a woman is tearful and anxious but sleeps when the baby sleeps, is caring for him well and has no thoughts of harm. The most likely diagnosis is [___].
cards.context:
Transient tearfulness, irritability and anxiety in the first postnatal week are common and resolve without treatment.

Persistence beyond 2 weeks, inability to function or thoughts of harm need assessment for depression.

cards.front: A woman who is pregnant for the first time is a [___].
cards.context:
Gravidity counts pregnancies of any outcome, including the current one, miscarriages, terminations and ectopic pregnancies.

So G1 means this is her first pregnancy; nothing about births is implied.

cards.front: Postnatal mood spectrum: baby blues peak at days 3-5 and self-resolve; postnatal depression can develop in the first year after birth. Screen with [___].
cards.context:
Postnatal mood disorders vary by timing, severity and loss of reality testing.

Baby blues affect 70-80%, peak around days 3-5 and usually resolve with support.

Postnatal depression can develop during the first year; onset varies. Screen with EPDS ([COPE guideline](https://www.cope.org.au/health-professionals/perinatal-mental-health-disorders/perinatal-depression)).

cards.front: Outpatient pelvic inflammatory disease (PID) empirical antibiotics: [___] (gonorrhoea) + doxycycline (chlamydia) + metronidazole (anaerobes).
cards.context:
PID is polymicrobial (Neisseria gonorrhoeae, Chlamydia trachomatis, Mycoplasma genitalium, anaerobes); empirical antibiotics must cover all: ceftriaxone (gonorrhoea) + doxycycline (chlamydia) + metronidazole (anaerobes).

Threshold to treat is deliberately low (CDC): any sexually active woman with pelvic pain + cervical motion tenderness OR uterine tenderness OR adnexal tenderness — start treatment.

Most managed as outpatients (oral, review at 72 h); admit for IV if pregnant, severe, suspected tubo-ovarian abscess, no response to oral, or unable to tolerate oral. Sexual partner notification + treatment essential.

cards.front: At 39 weeks, a woman's membranes rupture with a gush of bright red blood. She has no pain, pulse 80, and a fundal placenta on her 20-week scan. The fetal heart falls to 70/min. The likely cause is [___].
cards.context:
The blood lost is fetal, from an unprotected vessel crossing the membranes near the cervix. A fetus has little blood to lose, so the heart rate falls within minutes while the mother stays well.

Undiagnosed, perinatal mortality is 44–70%. The response is immediate birth: category 1 caesarean, or instrumental birth if she is fully dilated.

cards.front: Constipation in pregnancy is largely caused by [___] slowing gut transit.
cards.context:
Progesterone relaxes smooth muscle throughout the body. In the gut this slows transit and loosens the lower oesophageal sphincter.

The same relaxation of the ureters contributes to their dilatation in pregnancy.

cards.front: EPDS interpretation thresholds: a total score of 13 is the cut-off for probable depression (full psychiatric assessment); scores of 10-12 are possible cases (repeat in 2-4 weeks); a positive response on the dedicated [___] item triggers immediate safety assessment regardless of total score.
cards.context:
EPDS is a 10-item self-report questionnaire (scored 0-30) validated for antenatal + postnatal screening.

Interpretation: <10 = low risk, routine follow-up; 10-12 = possible, repeat in 2-4 weeks; ≥13 = probable, full psychiatric assessment.

cards.front: When two or more repeat bloodspot indications apply, besides the routine sample, a [___] decides the collection timing.
cards.context:
Transfusion, birth weight under 1500 g, and unmet milk-feed criteria each have a different repeat interval. The routine spot at 48–72 hours still stands.

The guideline does not add those clocks into one date. If two or more extra indications apply, a neonatologist sets the timing.

cards.front: The main hormone of the corpus luteum, which prepares the endometrium for implantation, is [___].
cards.context:
After ovulation the emptied follicle fills with lutein cells and becomes the corpus luteum. Its progesterone turns the endometrium secretory and ready for implantation.

Without hCG from a pregnancy, it regresses after about two weeks and the progesterone fall triggers menstruation.

cards.front: Pre-eclampsia diagnosis: HTN >20 weeks plus proteinuria (≥300 mg/24h or spot urine protein:creatinine ratio ≥[___] mg/mmol) OR end-organ dysfunction.
cards.context:
2018 ISSHP/SOMANZ expanded the pre-eclampsia definition — older 'HTN + proteinuria' missed ~20% of cases.

Spot PCR has largely replaced 24-hour collection — same accuracy, far more practical. The end-organ criterion catches 'pre-eclampsia without proteinuria' cases missed by the older definition.

cards.front: Labour requires three components: regular painful contractions with progressive cervical effacement and [___].
cards.context:
The diagnostic criteria for labour are deliberately strict: REGULAR (timed, recurring), PAINFUL contractions with PROGRESSIVE cervical change.

Braxton-Hicks contractions are irregular and usually painless, without progressive cervical change. Latent-phase contractions may be painful and irregular.

Painful contractions without demonstrated cervical change need assessment and sometimes reassessment. They may represent early labour or false labour; discharge depends on maternal and fetal wellbeing.

cards.front: Pre-eclampsia diagnosis: HTN >20 weeks plus proteinuria (≥[___] mg/24h or spot urine protein:creatinine ratio ≥30 mg/mmol) OR end-organ dysfunction.
cards.context:
2018 ISSHP/SOMANZ expanded the pre-eclampsia definition — older 'HTN + proteinuria' missed ~20% of cases.

Spot PCR has largely replaced 24-hour collection — same accuracy, far more practical. The end-organ criterion catches 'pre-eclampsia without proteinuria' cases missed by the older definition.

cards.front: Pelvic pain from altered nociception, without clear tissue damage or a somatosensory lesion, is [___] pain.
cards.context:
Nociceptive pain comes from actual or threatened damage to tissue. Neuropathic pain comes from a lesion or disease of the sensory nerves.

This third pattern is a more sensitive warning system. Pain continues although no new tissue damage is found, which is why another laparoscopy may not help.

cards.front: The four Ts of postpartum haemorrhage are [___], trauma, tissue and thrombin.
cards.context: NSW PPH guidance: the four categories structure cause assessment while resuscitation continues. More than one cause may be present, so finding atony does not end the assessment.

cards.front: A one-sided postnatal calf larger than the other leg by more than [___] is listed as a deep vein thrombosis feature.
cards.context:
Swelling after birth is often mild and on both sides. The flowchart marks thrombosis when one calf is larger by more than 2 cm, with pain, warmth or pitting.

The same row includes prominent superficial veins. Those veins do not make a separate harmless diagnosis when the calf is also swollen.

The table says a calf or thigh increase particularly if 2 cm or more. A difference of more than 2 cm meets both wordings.

cards.front: Pre-eclampsia diagnosis requires hypertension after [___] weeks PLUS new organ involvement (renal, hepatic, haematological, neurological, pulmonary, or placental).
cards.context:
2018 ISSHP/SOMANZ broadened pre-eclampsia from 'HTN + proteinuria' to 'HTN + ANY new organ involvement' — ~20% of pre-eclampsia has no significant proteinuria but still has organ dysfunction.

Every visit after 20 weeks checks blood pressure, symptoms and urine protein. Creatinine, LFTs and FBC follow when hypertension or symptoms appear.

cards.front: The baby of an HBsAg-positive mother gets hepatitis B vaccine plus hepatitis B [___] at birth.
cards.context:
Immunoglobulin gives ready-made antibody straight away; the vaccine starts the baby making its own.

Both are given as soon as possible after birth, ideally within 12 hours, in different thighs. The baby then completes the routine hepatitis B schedule.

cards.front: The classic primary lesion of syphilis is a single painless [___] at the site of inoculation, which heals on its own.
cards.context:
Primary syphilis classically causes a single painless ulcer (chancre), but lesions can be multiple or painful. The ulcer heals without treatment; the infection does not.

Secondary syphilis may cause a palm-and-sole rash, fever and lymphadenopathy. Late disease can cause gummas or aortitis. Neurosyphilis can occur at any stage, including early infection.

Australia is in a syphilis epidemic, and congenital syphilis has returned, which is why every pregnant woman is screened at booking.
